question: In what way is the soul identified here as both more supreme and as the haṃsa who is power joined to an individual?
premises: That soul is more supreme than some other term.
The one who is more supreme is he.
That same one is the haṃsa, power joined to an individual.
inference: The soul is the more supreme one who is the haṃsa, identified as power joined to an individual.
uncertainties: Precise distinction from other principles not stated
plain_english: He is the soul, more supreme. Indeed, he is the haṃsa, power joined to an individual.
